Good afternoon!
I really like Lean, but at the same time, I really like a programming language to be fast.
Could you please tell me if there's any way to evaluate Lean's speed?
In your personal experience, how does it compare to other languages?
Gemini highly praised the Perseus algorithm, which Lean uses for garbage collection.
Have you tried searching for performance comparisons of Lean with other languages? What were the results of such a search?

Also, "fast" can have multiple meanings --- runtime performance of generated code, compilation times, end-to-end development time for a first version, end-to-end-development time for a fast version, etc. It may help to specify what exactly you're interested in; that also allows you to search better.

Filipp said:

Gemini highly praised the Perseus algorithm, which Lean uses for garbage collection.

This is muddled. I think more accurate is to say the Perceus was inspired by Lean. Also it seems a little silly to call either Lean's or Perceus' operation "garbage collection", since the whole point is there is never any garbage.

Reference counted garbage collection is still garbage collection.

In this case, the perceus paper is explicit about not providing a cycle collector and "mitigates" cycles rather than solving them.

A colleague suggested different speed criteria:
1) Compiled binary execution speed
2) Compilation speed
3) Standard program development speed
4) Program development speed optimized for execution speed

How would you rate Lean in all these aspects? Does it perform well?

General advice: don't ask huge open ended questions without providing some evidence you've already thought about it yourself. What have you learnt from your research? What specifically would you like to learn more about?
Hmm... Has anyone seen any benchmarks? Could you share a link?
